title: Predicting Crime by Location: Spatial Hotspots & KDE Analysis
simple_summary: Why do crimes happen in specific places? Criminals look for easy getaways, crowds, and blind spots. By turning scattered incident pins into a smooth 200m-300m heat bubble, police see where risk clusters without guessing.
key_concept: Kernel Density Estimation (KDE): Rather than looking at single addresses, we smooth points into density zones. A moving hotspot is more actionable than a static one.
recommended_action: 10-15 minute high-visibility patrol stops at peak risk corners during forecasted hours.

dataset_sample.primary_attractor: High transit footfall + narrow bottleneck lane
Poor street lighting after 9 PM, blind curve

non_tech_takeaway: Never spread police thinly everywhere like butter. Concentrate short, visible 10-15 minute visits on the top 5% hotspot intersections to deter 50% of opportunistic crimes.
